articles.title: Nations League: Kylian Mbappé injured after scoring France winner in Turkey
articles.summary: France beat 10-man Turkey 1-0 to start Zidane era. Italy 0-2 Belgium, Georgia 0-1 Northern Ireland. Kylian Mbappé limped off with an apparent knee injury, moments after scoring France’s winner against Turkey in the Nations League on Friday.
body: The Real Madrid striker rifled in a low shot in the 55th minute after he was set up by Michael Olise. Soon after his record-extending 67th France goal, Mbappé sat on the ground and grimaced as he rubbed the area around his left knee.

The new France head coach, Zinedine Zidane, replaced Mbappé with Désiré Doué. In an encouraging sight, he was able to walk off the field of his own accord – but Zidane said afterwards that he expects his captain to return to Real Madrid for treatment.

“It’s not great. Unfortunately I think he [Mbappé] is going to have to go home. We don’t want to take any risks,” Zidane told French broadcaster TF1. “He overextended his knee while shooting. It’s not very encouraging.”

Jules Koundé hit the post for France before Turkey were reduced to 10 men, goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir sent off for handling the ball outside his area after Bradley Barcola had been played through on goal.

articles.title: International team lead US in Presidents Cup
articles.summary: The International team produce a brilliant fightback in the foursomes on day two of the Presidents Cup to take a 7-3 lead over the United States.
body: The US had been 3-2 up after the fourballs on Thursday but in a stunning turnaround were beaten in all five matches in the alternate-shot format in Medinah on Friday.
It boosted their hopes of a first victory in the event since 1998 and only a second since the competition began in 1994.
Geoff Ogilvy's side secured their first point of the day as Sungjae Im and Hideki Matsuyama saw off Russell Henley and Jacob Bridgeman 3&2.
Canadian duo Corey Conners and Nick Taylor then produced a stunning result as they held on to beat world number one Scottie Scheffler and Sam Burns by one hole.

articles.title: Manchester City guilty verdict ‘a historic decision’, says whistleblower Rui Pinto
articles.summary: Football Leaks founder’s information triggered probes. Has faced legal issues and lives under police protection. Years after his leaks shook the foundations of European football, Rui Pinto is claiming vindication following Manchester City’s conviction for financial fair play breaches.
body: Pinto, whose leaks of private documents helped trigger investigations into Manchester City’s financial affairs, has spoken about the club’s recent conviction for breaching financial fair play rules in a statement sent to the Guardian and later posted on social media.

Calling the conviction a “historic decision for English football”, Pinto said the ruling vindicates the vast repository of internal emails and financial records he leaked, material that helped trigger investigations by both Uefa and the Premier League.

According to Pinto, the findings demonstrate that Manchester City did not simply bend financial fair play regulations, but systematically undermined them through what he described as “structural manipulation and financial manoeuvring”, reducing the governing rules to a “mere formality”.

“That meticulously orchestrated fraud will finally be subject to punishment, and the impact will not merely be turbulent, but truly devastating for the Cityzens,” he said. Manchester City maintain their innocence and are expected to appeal.

articles.title: Andy Robertson says players are ‘not to blame’ for Manchester City’s actions
articles.summary: City found guilty of breaching Premier League rules. Liverpool finished second to City in 2019 and 2022. The former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson believes trophy-winning Manchester City players should not have their achievements diminished or removed because of the actions of the club’s…
body: Robertson was flying from a training camp in Spain to Slovenia with the Scotland squad when news emerged that City have been found guilty of multiple breaches of the Premier League’s financial fair play rules. The Scotland captain, who regularly jousted with City during his nine years at Anfield from 2017, was taken aback when news of the upcoming verdict was put to him in Ljubljana.

With the Premier League likely to penalise City heavily – it is understood the club intend to appeal against a guilty verdict – retrospective trophy removal has been cited as a potential punishment. Robertson made clear he sees little merit in that.

“For me, the players showed they were good enough on the pitch,” said the 32-year-old. “I don’t know too much about the charges and stuff like that. But they had an incredible team, one that I loved battling against. I don’t think when it comes to these things that players are ever to blame. That’s all I can focus on”.
Robertson’s former Liverpool manager, Jürgen Klopp, said he would throw a party if City had silverware removed.

articles.title: Rodri believes in Man City's 'innocence'
articles.summary: Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri believes the club are innocent of any financial wrongdoing and will trust them unless they are proved otherwise.
body: City have been found guilty of breaking the majority of the 115 financial rules they were accused of breaching by the Premier League, although they are set to appeal.
Speaking at a news conference before Spain's Uefa Nations League match against England at Wembley the 30-year-old, who joined Barcelona in August, backed City's stance.
"They always express the confidence that they never did something wrong and we believe in that," Rodri said.
"Until the moment they are proved wrong, we will believe the club. They always tell us the confidence they have on the innocence."

articles.summary: Connacht fall to an opening-night defeat in the United Rugby Championship in Galway as the Stormers' power wore them down in the second half.
body: After a slow start to the opening 40 minutes, two quick-fire tries for the hosts turned the game on its head in the dying minutes of the first half.
However, a brilliant display of strength and game management from the Stormers meant that the points would be leaving with the South Africans after the first game of the new season.

The visitors started the game in fast fashion when Ruhan Nel almost touched down after six minutes, were it not for Ireland back Mack Hansen's last-ditch tackle to make sure the scores stayed level, before Jurie Matthee kicked between the posts to open the scoring for the evening.

Things would get worse for the Westerners when Warrick Gelant crossed for the first try of the game, when he chased a well-weighted kick after a period of pressure on the left wing for the Stormers, and Matthee slotted over the conversion.

articles.title: What comes after 30-30 season even bigger for Elly De La Cruz, Reds
articles.summary: TORONTO – As if everybody in Cincinnati didn’t already how thoroughly the Reds have wasted the first 3 1/2 years of Elly De La Cruz’s limited time in a Reds uniform, the franchise’s most dynamic performer since Eric Davis emphasized the point in the season’s final series.
body: The shortstop who hit for the cycle in his 15th career game and stole third and home on one pitch in his 29th, finished off a rare 30-30 season with two games left in his third full season in the majors.

One night after hitting a no-doubt shot to right in Atlanta for his 30th home run of the season, De La Cruz doubled home two runs, then stole third base on the next pitch for steal No. 30 in the third inning in Toronto.

The throw wasn’t close as De La Cruz joined Davis (1987), Barry Larkin (1996) and Brandon Phillips (2007) among only four players in franchise history to achieve that milestone – 52nd in major-league history.

The way De La Cruz burst on the scene in 2023 – with best-in-the-game speed and power that included a 458-foot home run in his second game – a 30-30 season looked not only inevitable but perennial for the 21-year-old phenom.

articles.title: Spencer Torkelson slugs, steals JV's show as Tigers outlast Pirates
articles.summary: Detroit Tigers score: Spencer Torkelson finished a single short of the cycle and reached base on a strikeout as the Tigers capitalized on Bucs flubs.
body: The Detroit Tigers almost blew a big lead handed to them by first baseman Spencer Torkelson, but held off the late-inning rally.

With two-out RBI hits from Torkelson and catcher Dillon Dingler, plus some defensive miscues from the visitors, the Tigers (75-85) beat the Pittsburgh Pirates, 8-7, on Saturday, Sept. 25, at Comerica Park in Detroit. Torkelson's two-RBI triple in the second inning erased a 2-0 Tigers deficit, while Dingler gave the Tigers the lead with his two-out, bases-loaded single in the third.

Detroit tacked on more runs in the third thanks to a dropped-third strike leading to two extra runs, and then a two-out error from Pirates phenom Konnor Griffin in the sixth inning led to Detroit's seventh run. Torkelson, who finished a single away from the cycle – and was on deck for the final out of the eighth inning – added a solo home run in the seventh inning that gave the Tigers an 8-2 lead.

Staked to a six-run lead, lefty Andrew Sears gave up five runs in the eighth inning to make the score 8-7, but closer Kenley Jansen pitched a scoreless ninth to seal the win and record his 498th career save.

With Major Applewhite bringing his Group of 6 South Alabama squad to Kroger Field for a 12:45 p.m. ET kickoff this Saturday on the SEC Network, the setup has all the makings of a classic trap game.

articles.title: Northampton, Bath begin Prem season with crushing wins as Pollock sports new hair
articles.summary: Friday's opening night of the Prem Rugby season sees defending champions Northampton Saints and Bath post crushing wins over Newcastle Red Bulls and Harlequins...
body: Tommy Freeman and James Pater scored hat-tricks as Northampton, the reigning Prem champions, took advantage of a favourable opening fixture to record a convincing victory over last season's bottom club.

Since the end of last season, Newcastle Red Bulls have recruited extensively and they did show signs of improvement but it was a tough ask against a side making a statement of their intention to fiercely defend their title.
Tries from George Hendy, Alex Coles and Ollie Sleightholme took Saints' tally to nine with Fin Smith adding five conversions and Anthony Belleau two.

Christian Wade scored two tries for the visitors to take his Premiership tally to 95 - just six behind the record holder Chris Ashton. Cam Jordan and Werner Kok were the other try-scorers with two conversions coming from Zack Henry and one from Brett Connon.

articles.title: Yankees Retire Hall of Famer CC Sabathia's No. 52, Gets Monument Park Plaque
articles.summary: CC Sabathia saw many ceremonies honoring former players during 11 seasons with the New York Yankees and never envisioned he would be an honoree. Sabathia became the 24th player or manager to get his number retired and the Hall of Fame left-hander was honored with a plaque in Monument Park during a…
body: Sabathia joined Derek Jeter, Mariano Rivera, Andy Pettitte and Jorge Posada as the fifth member of 2009 World Series champion Yankees with a retired number and plaque.

"I never envisioned myself going into Monument Park and I think that was the reason why I was so scared to come here is because you don’t ever think you’re going to win the Yankee fans over or the city over," Sabathia said. "So to be able to be sitting here now, playing here 11 years is an incredible feeling and that’s why I’ve said the last couple of weeks, this feels bigger to me than the Hall of Fame because I know what was at stake when I came here."

Now 46, Sabathia signed a $161 million, seven-year contract before the 2009 season after being convinced by general manager Brian Cashman following an initial meeting in December 2008. The contract was the largest at the time for a free-agent pitcher.

Sabathia went 19-8 with a 3.37 ERA in 34 starts for the Yankees in his first season. He earned the AL Championship Series MVP Award, going 2-0 with a 1.13 ERA in a six-game win over the Los Angeles Angels and started Games 1 and 4 as the Yankees beat Philadelphia for their 27th title.
